This chapter translates neural network concepts into production frameworks:

- **scikit-learn** — `MLPClassifier` with standard `fit/predict` interface [@pedregosa2011scikit].
- **PyTorch** — Dynamic computational graphs and object-oriented automatic differentiation [@paszke2019pytorch].
- **JAX** — Pure functional paradigm with explicit PRNG, vectorization, and XLA compilation [@bradbury2018jax; @heek2023flax; @deepmind2020optax].

## Deep Learning Framework Ecosystem {#sec-ecosistema}

| Framework | Paradigm | Primary Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| scikit-learn | Object-Oriented High-Level | Small tabular data baselines |
| PyTorch | Imperative / Dynamic Graph | General deep learning & research standard |
| JAX | Pure Functional / XLA JIT | High-order differentiation & TPU acceleration |

```python
from sklearn.neural_network import MLPClassifier
from sklearn.datasets import make_moons

X, y = make_moons(n_samples=400, noise=0.2, random_state=42)
clf = MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(16, 16), max_iter=500, random_state=42)
clf.fit(X, y)
print(f"Accuracy: {clf.score(X, y):.3f}")
```

## PyTorch Fundamentals {#sec-pytorch-fundamentos}

### Tensors and Autograd

$$
\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \theta} \quad \forall \theta \text{ with } \texttt{requires\_grad=True}
$$ {#eq-autograd}

`loss.backward()` computes gradients automatically via chain rule backpropagation across dynamic computation graphs.

```{=html}

<script>
(function(){
  var current = 1, total = 5;
  function activate(step) {
    current = step;
    document.querySelectorAll(".pt-panel").forEach(p => p.style.display = p.dataset.step == step ? "block" : "none");
    document.querySelectorAll(".pt-tab").forEach(t => t.style.color = t.dataset.step == step ? "#0d6efd" : "#495057");
    document.getElementById("pt-counter").textContent = "Step " + step + " / " + total;

  window.ptNav = function(dir) { activate(Math.min(Math.max(current + dir, 1), total)); };
  document.querySelectorAll(".pt-tab").forEach(t => t.addEventListener("click", function(){ activate(+this.dataset.step); }));
  activate(1);
})();
</script>
```

Numerically stable Binary Cross Entropy with Logits Loss:

$$
\mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left[ \max(z_i, 0) - z_i y_i + \log\left(1 + e^{-|z_i|}\right) \right]
$$ {#eq-bceloss}

## JAX Fundamentals {#sec-jax-fundamentos}

JAX relies on pure functions and stateless pytrees.

```{=html}
<div style="border:1px solid #dee2e6;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;margin:1.5em 0;">
  <div style="display:flex;background:#f8f9fa;border-bottom:1px solid #dee2e6;">
    <button id="jax-tab-pt" onclick="jaxToggle('pt')" style="flex:1;padding:.7em;border:none;background:none;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;color:#ef553b;">PyTorch — Imperative</button>
    <button id="jax-tab-jax" onclick="jaxToggle('jax')" style="flex:1;padding:.7em;border:none;background:none;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;color:#6c757d;">JAX — Functional</button>
  </div>
  <div id="jax-panel-pt" style="padding:1.2em 1.5em;">
    <p style="margin:0;font-size:.9em;color:#555;">Mutable object-oriented model encapsulation holding parameters internally.</p>
  </div>
  <div id="jax-panel-jax" style="display:none;padding:1.2em 1.5em;">
    <p style="margin:0;font-size:.9em;color:#555;">Stateless pure functions receiving parameters externally as explicit pytree dictionaries.</p>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
function jaxToggle(which) {
  var isPT = which === 'pt';
  document.getElementById('jax-panel-pt').style.display = isPT ? 'block' : 'none';
  document.getElementById('jax-panel-jax').style.display = isPT ? 'none' : 'block';
}
</script>
```

Single-instance scalar Binary Cross Entropy in JAX:

$$
\mathcal{L}(w) = -\left[ y \log \sigma(wx) + (1-y) \log(1 - \sigma(wx)) \right]
$$ {#eq-bce-jax}

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
import optax

def loss_fn(params, x, y):
    logits = forward(params, x)
    return optax.sigmoid_binary_cross_entropy(logits, y).mean()

@jax.jit
def train_step(params, opt_state, x, y):
    loss, grads = jax.value_and_grad(loss_fn)(params, x, y)
    updates, new_opt_state = optimizer.update(grads, opt_state, params)
    new_params = optax.apply_updates(params, updates)
    return new_params, new_opt_state, loss
```

## Summary

PyTorch provides an intuitive, object-oriented imperative workflow ideal for rapid prototyping and debugging. JAX enforces pure functional programming, enabling high-order automatic differentiation and JIT compilation via XLA [@paszke2019pytorch; @bradbury2018jax].
